advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add reconciler-level tests for `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity`: assignee-with-accountId mints a jira/accountId ghost, assignee-without-accountId mints nothing, and a mint failure does not fail the inbound CREATE/EDIT apply.
evidence: search_files for `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` returns only the 3 definition/call sites in apply_inbound_records.py — no test file references it
Docstring claims 'no accountId or any mint failure is swallowed and the apply continues with the name-only behavior' (lines 57-59) — none of these branches are covered
apply_inbound.py:156 now forwards `repo_root` into the EDIT path solely for this feature; a regression to None would resolve/mint against the wrong root undetected
advisory.finding: The inbound reconciler wiring `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` and its two call sites (_inbound_create_write_create_event line 144, _inbound_update_write_edit_event line 302) have no tests. The behaviors introduced by the diff — assignee-with-accountId mints/reuses a jira-keyed ghost, assignee-without-accountId mints nothing and continues name-only, and a mint failure is swallowed without failing the apply — are all unexercised.
scenarios: An inbound Jira create/update with an assignee carrying accountId should produce a placeholder identity
An inbound assignee dict lacking accountId must not mint anything and must not fail the apply
An ensure_identity_for exception must not abort the inbound CREATE/EDIT event write

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_reuses_existing_real_identity, assert the real identity's title remains 'Real Ada' (not overwritten to the inbound display_name).
evidence: Test asserts `got == real`, `_mapping_count == 1`, and `is_placeholder(real) is False` (lines 79-82) but never checks the title stays 'Real Ada'

Inbound display_name is 'Ada From Jira' (line 78); the upgrade branch guarded by `is_placeholder(existing)` at identity.py:336 is what prevents the rename — removing it leaves this assertion set green
advisory.finding: test_reuses_existing_real_identity does not assert the real identity's title is left unchanged, so it cannot detect a regression of the diff's core invariant ('NEVER overwriting a real identity's name'). Removing the `is_placeholder(existing)` guard on the upgrade branch would rename the real identity to the inbound display_name and this test would still pass.
scenarios: A real (non-placeholder) identity mapping the accountId receives an inbound resolve with a different display_name

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that ensure_identity_for with an empty display_name mints a placeholder titled with the external_id.
evidence: Mint path uses `(display_name or '').strip() or external_id` (line 352) — a distinct documented branch
No test passes an empty/whitespace display_name to ensure_identity_for on the mint path (search of both test files shows only non-empty names)
advisory.finding: The documented blank-display_name mint fallback (title becomes external_id when display_name is empty) has no test.
scenarios: An inbound user with no display_name mints a placeholder whose title falls back to the external_id
